#5161. Revolut Lists GoMining Token for UK and European Users

Home » Exchanges » Revolut Lists GoMining Token for UK and European Users

The move brings the niche utility token to more than 15 million fintech app users under the EU’s MiCA regulatory framework.

Retail fintech giant Revolut has added GOMINING, the native utility token of the digital Bitcoin mining platform GoMining, to its in-app cryptocurrency trading service. The listing enables over 15 million Revolut crypto users across the United Kingdom and the European Economic Area (EEA) to buy, hold, and trade the token alongside everyday banking services.

Prior to this integration, GOMINING was primarily accessible through crypto-native exchanges such as Kraken, KuCoin, and Bitget.

The listing builds on an existing payment integration established in 2024 that allowed European users to fund GoMining accounts via Revolut Pay. It also adds GOMINING to Revolut’s cryptocurrency trading service.

Revolut reviews digital assets before listing them, assessing their risks, compliance requirements and potential financial crime exposure. It also monitors listed tokens on an ongoing basis as part of its procedures under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).

“For years, there has been a clear line between crypto and traditional finance, and most people stayed on one side of it,” said Mark Zalan, CEO of GoMining, in a statement announcing the listing. “For GoMining, this listing means our token is no longer only for people who already live in the crypto world.”

GOMINING has several uses within the GoMining platform. Token holders can use it to pay digital miner maintenance fees, with discounts of up to 20%, buy digital miners on the platform’s marketplace and purchase boosts in Miner Wars, GoMining’s mining game.

The token also has a governance function. Users can lock their GOMINING tokens to receive veGOMINING, which gives them voting rights on the allocation of ecosystem rewards.

Revolut customers can now buy GOMINING directly through the app. To use the token on GoMining, they must first transfer it to an external GoMining account.

The Revolut listing gives GOMINING exposure to a wider retail audience through a mainstream financial app. It also provides another way for users to acquire the token without first opening an account on a crypto-native exchange.

However, buying GOMINING through Revolut does not provide direct access to GoMining’s platform features. Users must transfer their tokens to an external wallet before using them within the GoMining ecosystem.

#5160. 17 Years Ago, Satoshi Nakamoto Opens His BitcoinTalk Account: What Happened Next

On this day, 17 years ago, Satoshi Nakamoto opened an account on BitcoinTalk, the place that would become the home of early Bitcoin enthusiasts and then turn into a public forum for crypto in general, until social media platforms took over the internet.

The network itself was barely 1 year old, and its future raised more questions than answers. Satoshi Nakamoto welcomed users on the forum and invited any questions people had regarding the cryptocurrency.

In 2010, the revolution began: 10,000 BTC was used to buy two pizzas, one of the first uses of the digital asset in exchange for a commodity. In May, Laszlo Hanyecz probably had the most expensive pizza dinner in history, considering how much BTC rallied after that. By December, Satoshi made their final BitcoinTalk post and announced their farewell.

The 2011-2014 period turned out to be the foundation for the network as a whole. Bitcoin became an open-source project maintained by others. The first halving happened in November 2012 and reduced the block issuance from 50 to 25 BTC per block.

The first-ever exchange implosion, Mt.Gox in 2014, raised serious questions about the security and stability of centralized exchanges, an issue we haven't solved 17 years later.

2017-2021 were the years when the industry truly blossomed. We had our first bull run on Bitcoin, which pushed the price above expected levels, to almost $20,000 in December 2017, along with the first altcoin bull run and the birth of new technologies like smart contracts, NFTs and many more. The next cycle took Bitcoin to around $69,000 in November 2021.

However, with the growth of the industry, multiple conflicts arose around safety, integrity and usage. The first country in the world to adopt Bitcoin was El Salvador, which implemented the digital currency as a true means of payment, in addition to accumulating it in its treasury.

2022 was the pivotal year, marked by the FTX and Terra crashes that changed how investors treat markets in general. FTX wasn't just an exchange: it was the backbone of the cryptocurrency market in those years. It aimed to rival Binance and become the bridge between institutional investors and crypto.

However, poor risk management, issues with fund allocation and many other factors caused an implosion that ended the bull run.

In 2024, Wall Street arrived in crypto with ETFs, ETPs, perpetual futures and a regulatory framework. The digital assets industry became a part of a larger market. Whether that is good or bad is a question to consider, but one thing is clear: Bitcoin has come a very long way since 2010 and is evolving to this day.

The next step is the arrival of AI and rising cybersecurity risks, which go toe-to-toe with the quantum danger. How the first cryptocurrency handles them is a question that directly affects its future.

#5159. Cypherpunk Reports 8,967 ZEC Mined as Zcash Treasury Nears 342,000 Tokens

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Publicly traded Cypherpunk Technologies has reported the first results from its Zcash mining operation, producing 8,967.29 ZEC in just 44 days. The company says those tokens represented approximately $9.9 million of mining revenue in the third quarter, while its treasury later grew to about 341,859 ZEC through purchases and continued production. The figures are impressive in isolation. But investors need to separate operating earnings from accounting gains on an appreciated token reserve, especially after ZEC’s volatile price action.

Cypherpunk’s November 16 filing says the mining fleet began operation on August 18 and delivered about 95% uptime through September 30. The company reported revenue corresponding to 8,967.29 ZEC, with a stated average cost of mining revenue of approximately $104 per token before depreciation. Once depreciation of equipment is included, the company reported a higher per-token cost near $237. The distinction is crucial when comparing mining economics across companies because machines lose value over time even if their near-term power and hosting costs look low.

Cypherpunk says holdings reached around 341,858.75 ZEC after adding October mining output and recent market purchases, equivalent to roughly 2% of the circulating supply at its reporting date. Its strategy therefore combines an operating mining business with a substantial asset inventory. Both components are sensitive to the cryptocurrency’s price. Tokens generated through mining may be held rather than sold to cover expenses, which can expand exposure and affect cash needs. A higher coin count is not the same as higher spendable cash in the company’s bank accounts.

For related context, see our earlier report on the recent Zcash NU7 protocol upgrade.

The Block reported approximately $2.6 million of quarterly operating profit and substantially greater net income driven by unrealized increases in the value of the ZEC treasury. Valuation gains can be economically relevant, but they can also reverse without an operational change. Investors should read the quarterly income statement and cash-flow statement together. A business with rising book profits may still need external financing to buy new equipment or meet operating expenses if it is retaining mined tokens. The source of earnings determines how repeatable they are.

The company says its fleet represented a material part of Zcash network hashrate at launch, while broader network competition has already changed that percentage. Management has discussed additional equipment purchases for 2027, subject to commitments and delivery. More hardware can produce more hashes, but miner returns depend on network difficulty, rewards, uptime, electricity and ZEC’s price. The most useful follow-up will compare actual production and operating cash with capital spent, rather than treating a treasury-size target as proof of long-term mining profitability.

Mining economics can shift even when a company executes its own operating plan well. As competitors add machines, a given fleet's fraction of network hashrate may fall, reducing expected token output at the same energy cost. Rewards also depend on protocol rules and equipment performance, while treasury purchasing introduces separate exposure to spot prices. Reporting those risks alongside current revenue helps readers understand why one profitable early period does not establish a permanent advantage. A full-year record will offer a stronger measure of the fleet's competitiveness.

For related context, see our earlier report on Bitcoin mining-difficulty changes.

Cypherpunk now has measurable mining output as well as a sizable ZEC balance. The challenge for investors is to value those as two connected but distinct businesses, avoiding the temptation to treat unrealized token appreciation as recurring operational income.

Reporting sources: Cypherpunk Q3 financial results, SEC exhibit · The Block coverage

Major crypto exchange Coinbase shared the options-implied seven-day ratios for major cryptocurrencies, highlighting that options traders might be preparing for an unusually large price move for XRP.

In an X post, Coinbase Markets shared the outcome of dividing the options-implied 7-day move by the median 7-day move for XRP, Bitcoin, Ethereum, and Solana.

Options-implied 7d move, divided by each asset's own median 7d move: $XRP 1.94× $BTC 1.69× $ETH 1.56× $SOL 1.46× $XRP is priced furthest above its own history, $SOL the least. Which one is asking for more than its own history delivered? https://t.co/WgWbqjcgwI

This suggests how much movement options markets are pricing in relative to each asset's own historical behavior. However, it does not compare their expected dollar or percentage moves directly.

According to the figures shared by Coinbase, XRP's options-implied seven-day move stands at 1.94 times its own historical median seven-day move. Bitcoin follows at 1.69 times, while Ethereum records 1.56 times and Solana comes in at 1.46 times.

XRP, therefore has the highest relative reading among the four assets, suggesting options traders are pricing in a more pronounced move than the token has typically delivered over a comparable period.

At the time of writing, XRP was down 1.93% in the last 24 hours to $0.98 amid the continued profit-taking in the market. XRP briefly reached $1 on November 18, 2026, but fell afterwards as traders took profits. XRP is down 21.57% so far in November, but its history says more than its current price action does.

XRP’s average November gain is skewed upward by massive outlier rallies—specifically +550% in 2013 and +282% in 2024. Its median November return is about -10%, meaning it has closed lower in most cycles in history. XRP dropped roughly 23.42% in November 2019 and lost 12.18% in November 2025 (opening at around $2.51 and closing at around $2.20).

A weak November doesn’t always mean a weak December: for instance, after falling 9.1% in November 2015, XRP jumped 46.8% in December 2015.

In the near term, XRP’s price recovery will target $1 before moving to the $1.24–$1.26 range. Alternatively, if the price falls further, it is likely to find support at $0.89.

Grayscale’s latest market note offers a two-part explanation for the sharp decline in crypto prices: money moving out of stablecoins and pressure spilling over from technology equities. Head of research Zach Pandl argues that fundamental adoption trends remain intact, even while Bitcoin and other large assets struggle. That is the assessment of an asset manager with a commercial interest in digital assets, not a settled finding that the sell-off is over. Its value lies in examining the mechanisms rather than repeating the optimistic conclusion as fact.

The November 16 research note points to accelerating withdrawals from stablecoins after the late-October Binance security incident. When investors redeem dollar-backed tokens for bank deposits, the supply of on-chain dollars can contract. That may reduce the liquidity available for trading and collateral, although it does not mean each redeemed dollar was about to buy Bitcoin. Other drivers can change supply, including arbitrage and issuer operations. Grayscale views off-ramping as one contributing factor to the November weakness. Confirming its influence requires tracking issuance, redemptions and market activity across venues.

The firm also identifies pressure in Nvidia and other AI-linked stocks as a possible source of portfolio de-risking. Investors holding growth technology and crypto exposure may sell both when financing conditions worsen or their risk limits tighten. There is a further link through physical infrastructure: some Bitcoin mining firms are developing high-performance computing services for AI operators. Those connections do not make Bitcoin a direct claim on AI company earnings. They suggest overlapping investors and capital requirements through which stress can travel across otherwise different sectors.

For related context, see our earlier report on stablecoin supply contraction.

Grayscale notes that Bitcoin fell below its 200-day moving average on November 12, a level followed by some trend-oriented trading strategies. Leveraged positions and thinner weekend order books can make subsequent price moves more abrupt. Those mechanisms may amplify a decline without identifying a single fundamental cause. Importantly, technical signals are not universal commands: different funds use different models and time horizons, and a moving-average breach does not determine the market’s next direction. The research describes a chain of plausible forces, not a proven one-factor explanation.

Grayscale believes medium- and long-term investors may find current valuations attractive because institutional stablecoin and tokenization activity continues to develop. The note also acknowledges inflation, interest-rate uncertainty and geopolitical risk. Those headwinds could persist longer than optimistic scenarios assume. Readers should distinguish the factual observation of a significant drawdown from the manager’s valuation judgment. ETF flows, stablecoin supplies and changes in rates can help test the thesis, but none offers a reliable standalone timing signal.

Another test of the explanation is whether on-chain capital actually returns when equity-market stress eases. A rebound in technology shares accompanied by ongoing stablecoin redemptions would suggest the factors are not moving in lockstep. In contrast, renewed stablecoin issuance without a broader Bitcoin recovery would show that liquidity availability alone is insufficient. Such cross-checks are more informative than assigning every daily price move to the same narrative. They also allow readers to separate Grayscale's interpretation from the specific market data used to support it.

For related context, see our earlier report on recent bitcoin ETF outflows.

The report provides a framework for thinking about November’s crypto decline, not proof that prices have bottomed. Its strongest contribution is highlighting how stablecoin redemptions, shared growth-stock positioning and leveraged market structure can interact during a difficult month.

#5152. Binance Hack-Linked Wallet Moves 34,279 ETH, but Investigators See No Confirmed Sale

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

A wallet linked by blockchain investigators to the October 29 Binance breach has transferred 34,279.66 ETH to three newly created addresses, ending a period of inactivity. The ether was worth roughly $63 million at prices used in Tuesday’s reporting. That is a significant movement of suspected stolen funds, but a wallet transfer is not automatically a sale, a successful laundering step or proof that the recipient controls are independent of the sender. Investigators had not identified the new addresses as exchanges at the time of their initial reports.

Monitoring groups MistTrack and Solid Intel reported the transfers on November 17. MistTrack described three movements of approximately 12,000 ETH, 12,000 ETH and 10,279.66 ETH. The receiving wallets were newly created, and the monitored funds had not moved again when the analysts published their findings. Public transaction records make it possible to trace the amounts and destinations, but they do not disclose the human operator behind each address. The link to the earlier breach rests on investigators’ attribution of the sending wallet, not a label embedded in the blockchain itself.

The October attack involved vastly larger losses than Tuesday’s movement. US investigators attributed the incident to a North Korean hacking group, and authorities have announced substantial asset restraints and seizures. Blockchain intelligence firms have also tracked funds moved through different assets and protocols. These parallel developments should not be added together casually, because frozen, seized, recovered and still-controlled amounts describe different legal and operational states. The fresh ETH transfers are one piece of a complex post-incident trail rather than an update to the full net-loss number.

For related context, see our earlier report on Coinbase's custody and security precautions.

Crypto trading commentary sometimes treats any transfer from an exploit-linked wallet as preparation to dump tokens. That can happen, but the evidence here does not yet establish a market sale. Transfers may consolidate funds, redistribute control or precede another operation. Until an address is linked to a trading venue, bridge, mixer or other service, the immediate observable fact is the destination change. Even a later exchange deposit would need careful interpretation: deposits are not identical to executed sell orders. Reporting should preserve those steps rather than collapsing them into one dramatic conclusion.

Ethereum’s public ledger lets investigators monitor known addresses and alert service providers if assets reappear at identifiable points. Token issuers, exchanges and law enforcement may each have different powers depending on the assets and jurisdictions involved. Native ETH cannot simply be frozen by an issuer in the way some centrally administered tokens can. That difference complicates recovery when funds leave services that can intervene. The next useful evidence will be further movements, identification of services receiving the funds and official updates to the case.

Investigators can improve attribution confidence by comparing the sequence, amounts and transaction timing with addresses already associated with the incident. Yet public labels can be incomplete, and a newly created wallet may simply be another address controlled by the same actor. Readers should resist claims that funds have reached a criminal group, a particular country or a cash-out desk unless that identification is supported by additional evidence. Future investigative notices should specify their degree of confidence and distinguish observed transfers from hypotheses about their purpose.

For related context, see our earlier report on the Unocoin wallet compromise.

The latest transfer warrants close monitoring, but it should not be reported as the disposal of $63 million in stolen ether without further proof. The distinction between observable transactions and inferred intent is especially important in a security incident of this scale.

Reporting sources: CoinDesk report of MistTrack and Solid Intel monitoring · MistTrack transfer report

On Nov. 18, Hong Kong's Securities and Futures Commission (SFC) added the decentralized exchange Hyperliquid to its list of suspicious virtual asset trading platforms. The listing covers the web interface of the Hyperliquid trading terminal at app.hyperliquid.xyz/trade. The HYPE token dropped to around $65.50 on the evening of Nov. 18, and it recovered to $68.79 by midday Nov. 19, according to TradingView data.

According to the entry, the company claims to provide digital asset trading services on the website, and it has no address on record. Hyperliquid is not licensed by the SFC, and it is suspected of operating a virtual asset trading platform in Hong Kong or actively promoting its services to the public, the regulator said.

In an accompanying warning, the SFC reminded investors that such platforms often lure users with "incredible investment opportunities." The SFC also reminded investors that clients of unlicensed platforms have no legal protection if a platform is hacked or misappropriates their assets.

On the same day, the Hyperliquid Policy Center (HPC) sent a letter to the U.K. Financial Conduct Authority with seven recommendations on the country's new crypto rules. "Regulatory obligations belong with persons who have unilateral control over a function that is a regulated activity," the group wrote.

On Nov. 16, two days before the SFC added Hyperliquid to the list, Hong Kong Financial Secretary Paul Chan spoke at the Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum. "Before the end of this year, we will introduce a bill to complete the regulatory perimeter," Chan said.

According to Chan, the bill will cover crypto dealers, custodians, advisers and asset managers. "Decentralisation does not mean less accountability," he said.

In April, the Hong Kong Monetary Authority licensed HSBC and Anchorpoint Financial as the first stablecoin issuers in the city, out of 36 applicants in the first round.

#5149. US Senators Question SEC Tokenized-Stock Exemption Over Wallet Transfers and Investor Protection

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Morbi pretium leo et nisl aliquam mollis. Quisque arcu lorem, ultricies quis pellentesque nec, ullamcorper eu odio.

Four Democratic US senators have pressed the Securities and Exchange Commission for answers about how its new approach to tokenized stock trading will protect investors and prevent illicit transfers. Their November 16 letter, reported by The Block, takes aim at gaps they see in the SEC’s five-year innovation exemption for certain trading venues. The development is an oversight challenge, not a court ruling or a notice that the exemption has been cancelled. It goes to a central difficulty for tokenized securities: a regulated purchase can become a blockchain transfer to another address.

The SEC introduced its approach in September, allowing qualifying tokenized-securities venues to operate under a defined exemption from some ordinary exchange-registration requirements. The aim is to permit experimentation with trading stocks in token form while the agency assesses a new market structure. A token representing a security still raises questions about ownership, trading rules and investor rights. The exemptions and their precise conditions matter more than a general statement that securities have moved on-chain. Not every blockchain token, broker or venue automatically qualifies for the same regulatory treatment.

Senators Angela Alsobrooks, Ruben Gallego, Mark Warner and Catherine Cortez Masto reportedly told SEC Chair Paul Atkins that the framework lacks sufficiently specific safeguards around know-your-customer and anti-money-laundering procedures. A buyer verified by a regulated venue might later transfer a token to a wallet whose controller has not undergone the same checks. This problem is not solved merely by verifying the identity of the first purchaser. The letter asks how secondary transfers and the reach of compliance obligations would be managed once tokens circulate beyond the initial venue.

For related context, see our earlier report on Hong Kong's developing licensing rules.

The senators raised concerns about retail-investor protections and pricing, and reportedly asked whether companies could opt out of having their shares tokenized. Those questions are distinct from financial-crime screening. A token that references equity needs a clear relationship to the rights and obligations of the underlying security, as well as fair information about execution and ownership. If an issuer’s wishes, the investor’s expectations and the platform’s legal structure do not line up, technical transferability alone cannot resolve the conflict. Policymakers must address those issues in enforceable terms.

The lawmakers asked the SEC to explain its approach and urged a transparent rulemaking process for changes in the regulatory treatment of tokenized securities. Such a letter can affect oversight and public debate, especially as control of congressional committees changes, but it is not itself binding legislation. Venues exploring tokenized equities should continue to follow the actual exemption terms and any subsequent SEC guidance. The next concrete milestones are the agency’s response, proposed revisions if any, and how early trading models implement identity, custody and transfer restrictions.

For related context, see our earlier report on new institutional crypto-custody arrangements.

Tokenization can change how securities move, but it does not automatically settle which rules should accompany them. The dispute now concerns the design of that regulatory perimeter, with no basis to describe the senators’ letter as an immediate prohibition on tokenized stocks.

Reporting sources: The Block report of four senators’ letter

the 16th of November, a federal judge acquitted Anton and James Peraire-Bueno in the “first of its kind” wire fraud prosecution over a $25 million Ethereum exploit. This judgement came about after the government failed to prove the brothers made any “material misrepresentation.”

The ruling, filed in the Southern District of New York (24-CR-293), came the same day as when Bitwise CEO Hunter Horsley pitched stablecoins as a backup for banks.

On a similar note, Ethereum [ETH] co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued that digital assets do not match up to investing in houses. These three developments, when taken together, compound the question of what crypto is actually for.

On the 2nd of April 2023, the brothers seemingly exploited a bug in the MEV-Boost relay software, due to which they could view transactions that sandwich traders believed were private.

The brothers’ alleged proposal for replacement transactions, in turn, resulted in massive losses of roughly $25 million within seconds.

Finally, on the 16th of November 2026, Judge Jessica G. L. Clarke, when granting an acquittal, wrote,

The question before the Court is not whether the Peraire-Buenos’ conduct was right or moral, or even whether it violated uncharged crimes.

It is simply whether the evidence at trial, construed in a light most favorable to the Government, could support wire fraud and related convictions in this case. Because the Government failed to prove that the Peraire-Buenos made any material misrepresentations in the execution of their scheme, the motion is granted.

The court analyzed the government’s theories – including the “lure transactions” and the so-called “false signature,” and found nothing that could support a wire fraud conviction.

A couple of days later, on the 18th of November, Horsley posted on X:

Rolling bank outages in the AI era – Consider having some stablecoins or crypto just in case.

The post came as thousands of Chase, Bank of America, and Wells Fargo customers reported being unable to access their accounts.

Vitalik Buterin, in a separate post on November 18, argued that younger generations have been investing in digital assets over real estate options; doing so, he noted, reduces –

Perverse incentives that drive people to push to keep housing expensive.

But he added a condition: housing had the advantage of being –

A culture and policy-encouraged default of investing in a safe non-crazy thing that you can’t easily liquidate.

Modern platforms encourage the opposite of this, leading to more irresponsible behavior… We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The three developments have been framing crypto’s developing role separately, but these assets have a long way to go before they can fully replace TradFi.

Vitalik Buterin himself leaves the question open, as he observed,

We need the equivalent of those good properties that housing investment has, for modern digital assets.

The ruling did not answer that question, nor did the outage.

#5145. Anthropic’s Record $81B IPO Is Here—Will It Test Crypto?

Home » Blitz news » Anthropic’s Record $81B IPO Is Here—Will It Test Crypto?

The Claude maker priced shares at $83 for a $1.5 trillion valuation as Bitcoin dips 1.5% ahead of Nasdaq trading.

Anthropic has priced its initial public offering (IPO) at $83 per share, raising roughly $81.3 billion in the largest public market debut in history—just as digital asset markets pull back and traders weigh whether the historic AI listing will siphon retail and institutional liquidity away from crypto.

According to Anthropic’s official announcement, the Claude AI developer priced its shares roughly 6.4% above its previously marketed range of $70 to $78, assigning the company a valuation of approximately $1.5 trillion. Trading on the Nasdaq under the ticker ANT is set to begin Thursday, November 19.

While Wall Street absorbed the massive tech offering, the broader cryptocurrency market traded lower on Thursday morning.

Total crypto market capitalization dropped 1.3% over the past 24 hours to $2.253 trillion, with Bitcoin (BTC) falling 1.5%, the most among the other top 10 biggest cryptos. Bitcoin is currently trading at $63,585.

Anthropic has expanded its IPO to 980 million shares, up from the initially planned 825 million, following exceptionally strong demand from institutional and retail investors.

Priced at $83 per share, the public offering is expected to raise approximately $81.3 billion, surpassing SpaceX’s $75 billion base offering in June and setting a new record.

The company is also raising an additional $26 billion through a private placement of non-voting shares, priced at the same $83 per share. Reported strategic investors include Nvidia, Microsoft, Google, AMD, Broadcom, Micron and TSMC. Combined, the public offering and private placement are expected to generate more than $107 billion.

Retail investors have been allocated up to 20% of the public offering, representing approximately $16.2 billion. Demand has been particularly strong, with total orders reportedly reaching nearly seven times the number of shares available, according to CNBC.

The deal values Anthropic at approximately $1.5 trillion, marking a dramatic increase from its $965 billion private valuation when it confidentially filed for an IPO in June.

Anthropic’s IPO could have implications for crypto markets beyond the AI sector. The $155 billion in combined IPO capital raised by SpaceX and Anthropic within five months highlights growing competition for institutional liquidity, potentially diverting funds from risk assets such as Bitcoin and altcoins.

The listing also gives retail investors a direct way to bet on AI, potentially reducing demand for crypto-native AI tokens that have attracted investors seeking similar exposure.

ANT’s market debut will also be closely watched as a gauge of risk appetite. A strong opening could lift sentiment across speculative assets, while a weak performance could reinforce risk-off sentiment in both equities and crypto.

#5144. How did Coinbase stop deepfake Elon Musk’s promise to double your crypto?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Scammers recently used a fake video of Elon Musk to get people to send them crypto. It didn’t go to plan.

Especially since according to Coinbase, it blocked a big chunk of those transfers before the money could disappear.

… and Coinbase stopped $4.7 million from reaching scammers.

Someone put out a YouTube livestream made to look like a Tesla flying car demo. On screen was an AI-made Elon Musk, and the pitch was to send crypto and get 2x back.

More than half a million people tuned in. The stream flashed wallet addresses and QR codes. So, sending money took just a scan.

In a blog post, Coinbase laid out what happened. In about two hours, hundreds of its users tried to send funds to the scammers. Its automated fraud system caught about 91% of that.

The real Musk had nothing to do with any of it.

Here, it’s worth pointing out that Coinbase hasn’t said how much of the remaining 9% actually got through.

Its fraud agent watches outgoing transfers as they happen.

If any transfer looks off or iffy, like a payment to a freshly created wallet or something tied to a “giveaway,” the agent in question steps in. In such a case, the agent opens a chat with the user, explains why the transfer might be risky, and prompts them to think twice before proceeding.

It even checks its own replies before showing them. According to Coinbase, no person was involved at any point. Nobody’s account got hacked either. No passwords leaked. People (some of them long-time users) chose to hit send because the fake Musk was convincing.

Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent.

That is exactly what makes these scams tough.

It isn’t the first fake Elon Musk either. A doctored video in 2023 reportedly cost victims around $160K. In June 2024, deepfake giveaways popped up on more than 35 YouTube channels during a Starship launch.

Binance will delist five crypto spot trading pairs within the next 24 hours on Nov. 20, 2026, following a review.

To protect its users and to ensure a high-quality trading market, Binance conducts regular reviews of all listed spot trading pairs; it may delist certain spot trading pairs for various reasons, including low liquidity and trading volume.

Binance will delist GAS/TRY, HBAR/BNB, HIVE/TRY, KSM/TRY and ZAMA/TRY pairs on November 20, 2026 at 03:00 UTC, according to an official announcement published on November 18.

Four of the five affected pairs are related to the Turkish lira (TRY), while the last one is HBAR/BNB. The decision affects trading between these specific assets and does not mean the cryptocurrencies themselves are being completely delisted from Binance.

The exchange clarified that users will still be able to trade the affected tokens through other available spot trading pairs on its platform.

Binance will terminate Spot Trading Bots services for the spot trading pairs simultaneously where applicable. Users are strongly advised to update and/or cancel their Spot Trading Bots prior to the cessation of services for Spot Trading Bots to avoid any potential losses.

In related news, Binance Margin will initiate a routine cleanup of Cross Margin accounts with collateral valued at less than 1 USD (or equivalent in other assets), effective from November 30, 2026 at 00:00 (UTC). The cleanup will be executed on a daily basis as an ongoing operational process.

Affected accounts include Cross Margin Accounts with a collateral value of less than 1 USD equivalent across all assets and no outstanding liabilities, as well as Margin Accounts with no capital activity in the past 6 months. Capital activity refers to any action that generates a capital flow.

For each eligible Small-Asset Account, the system will automatically transfer the collateral in users’ Margin Accounts to their Spot Accounts while the Margin Account functions remain normal, allowing users to transfer, borrow, or trade at any time after the cleanup.

Accounts with collateral equal to or exceeding 1 USD equivalent are not affected by this cleanup.

#5139. Dogecoin down by 44%, hits 2026’s lowest price — More downside ahead?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Dogecoin [DOGE] has been more bark than bite lately.

Last week’s sell-off pushed it down to a new yearly low on the charts and unfortunately, it doesn’t look like it’ll get back up anytime soon.

At the time of writing, Dogecoin was valued at $0.058. This followed a 3.3% dip over the day.

Things really fell apart on 14th November. DOGE fell from $0.065 to $0.057 in a single day. It also briefly hit $0.055, the lowest level of 2026. DOGE’s volume jumped too, implying that too many were selling at once.

Now, while it managed a small bounce to about $0.060 later, it wasn’t able to hold on to that level.

For context, DOGE was above $0.10 in late September. That’s 44% gone… in less than two months.

The RSI was at 28.9, hinting at oversold conditions. It even sank close to 18 during the crash. The MACD was still deep in the red, though the bars were shrinking just a tad.

Simply put, while the sellers seemed to be worn out, buyers are yet to show up.

Finally, leverage has been draining out too, with Open Interest sliding from about $475 million on the 11th to $362.5 at press time.

It is a nervous state of things, and one look at the funding rates will tell you why. It was red during the crash of the 14th, flipped a couple more times, and at press time was back to 0.0052%.

Some traders may be betting on a bounce again, but not in big numbers. Not yet.

ETFs have been even quieter. According to data from SoSoValue, Spot DOGE ETFs haven’t seen a single day of inflows or outflows since mid-October. A whole month of nothing.

Their total net assets still dropped though. We went from $17 million in late September to about $9.74 million at the time of writing. In simple words, Dogecoin’s falling price has been shrinking what’s already there.

#5138. NYSE owner targets Hyperliquid’s $5 billion trading boom, but the liquidity may not follow

Trade[XYZ] handles nearly 98% of HIP-3 trading volume, but ICE's planned US perpetual futures market must build its own pool of buyers and sellers.

Intercontinental Exchange (ICE), the New York Stock Exchange’s owner, is working with Trade[XYZ] to bring Hyperliquid-based perpetual futures to the US.

The proposed venue would have to attract its own buy and sell orders, Hyunsu Jung, CEO of Nasdaq-listed Hyperion DeFi, told CryptoSlate.

Jung said firms quoting on both the proposed US venue and existing overseas markets could help keep prices close if the venues match orders and handle funding similarly.

The amount a trader can buy or sell at those prices would depend on the orders available on the US market. Jung’s company builds on Hyperliquid and earns revenue from work in its ecosystem.

ICE announced the agreement on Oct. 29 and said it would be the exclusive operator of the regulated markets, using a dedicated retail venue and clearing structure separate from its institutional futures business.

ICE also announced a minority investment in Trade[XYZ], subject to regulatory approvals, including approvals needed to support leveraged trading. ICE’s announcement sets out who would operate and clear the market, leaving the trading rules and exact order-book design unspecified.

Perpetual futures let traders take positions on the price of a reference asset through a contract with no set expiration date. Trade[XYZ] already offers contracts on equities, stock indexes, commodities and currencies to eligible customers outside the US.

ICE expects customers who pass identity checks to access the proposed market through participating futures brokers, formally known as futures commission merchants, and also expects its joint venture with OKX to help distribute the contracts.

That route depends on separate approvals for the venture’s broker-dealer and futures commission merchant businesses.

The existing HIP-3 design gives each builder-deployed venue its own order books and margining on Hyperliquid’s shared trading infrastructure.

In its November quarterly filing, Hyperion DeFi described ICE and Trade[XYZ]’s plan in the context of HIP-3, an optional extension that lets operators control access. The filing tied the plans it discussed to regulatory approvals, finalizing the extension, and making it available on the live network.

An order book records what buyers and sellers are willing to trade at each price, so a buy order posted outside the US would be available to traders on that book. To complete a trade on a separate US venue, a customer would need a matching order on the US book.

Hyperliquid’s existing builder markets keep separate order books. ICE has proposed a US route for verified retail customers.

A separate US order book would need its own buy and sell orders.

ICE’s final order-book design remains unspecified. The proposed access route depends on regulatory approvals. The drawn orders are illustrative.

A schematic of Hyperliquid’s documented HIP-3 architecture alongside ICE’s proposed customer access route. The solid line indicates existing architecture, while dashed lines indicate the proposed US setup.

ICE’s final order-book design remains unspecified. The proposed access route depends on regulatory approvals. The drawn orders are illustrative.

If a comparable contract traded at a higher price on one venue, a firm able to trade both could buy on the cheaper venue and sell on the more expensive one. Those trades would tend to bring the two prices closer.

A market maker that takes the other side of a customer’s trade in the US could manage some of the resulting exposure overseas if it can access both venues.

Jung said margin and leverage rules for futures broker accounts would help determine how much liquidity firms can provide. Margin is the collateral a firm sets aside to support a position, and the more collateral a trade requires, the more of a firm’s capital it ties up.

Trade[XYZ] recorded over $4.9 billion of the $5 billion traded across tracked HIP-3 venues in the 24 hours through Nov. 18, representing 97.6% of the total. EntropyIO, the next-largest venue by volume, accounted for 2.3%, according to UnderHyper’s venue breakdown.

UnderHyper’s measure of rolling dollar volume counts completed trades across the HIP-3 venues it tracks.

Jung attributed Trade[XYZ]’s lead to listing key markets early and making them available in the Hyperliquid interface traders already used.

ICE hopes to reach US customers through brokers and distribution partners, but the size of that customer base and how often it trades will become clear only if the US venue opens.

If the US venue opens, traders will be able to judge its liquidity by the gap between the best buy and sell prices and how much they can trade near those prices. The test for ICE will come when traders try to move a large position near the price they first saw.

#5137. Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

Home » Exchanges » Trading Bots No Longer a Niche: Now It’s Web3’s Default

AI-powered trading tools are gradually becoming the default interface for Web3 trading, new research reveals.

A new report from Bitrue Research Institute tracks how trading bots have shifted from specialist software for technical users into everyday infrastructure across crypto markets.

The research paper combines public GitHub data on open-source projects, a survey of Bitrue users, and profiles of eight active bots to show where automation is heading.

Public GitHub activity shows a clear change in focus. New repositories describing themselves as “trading agents” jumped from 110 in 2024 to 1,133 in 2025 and reached 6,121 through November 15, 2026, more than five times the prior year’s total.

Classic crypto trading bot projects also grew sharply, rising from 551 in 2024 to 2,399 in 2025 (a 4.4× increase) with another 2,948 created so far in 2026.

The longest-running open-source tools still dominate stars: Freqtrade (56,933), Hummingbot (21,231), Jesse (8,807), and OctoBot (6,951).

An industry survey of 3,708 crypto traders published by MEXC in October 2026 found that 84.8% had used AI for research or trading in the previous six months, with 53.1% doing so at least weekly.

🤖 Here are more ways to earn with #BitrueAI!With #BitrueAI, select from a list of #crypto like #Bitcoin, #Solana and #XRP🔸 30 days backtested results🔸 Choose your own grid direction🔸 Customize your own settings with #BitrueAI👉 Start Now: https://t.co/3PW15XTAvd pic.twitter.com/ohHDBirMmQ

Among AI users, 34.6% had used an exchange’s own strategies or bots and 17.1% had connected an external agent.

On one major multi-exchange platform, average daily bot launches rose 29% from July to September 2026, reaching 862 per day, with real-fund launches up 36% and DCA bots up 80%.

The report identifies five structural changes:

In Bitrue’s survey of users who had not yet tried an AI trading bot, concern about losses and risk control was the top reason for hesitation (45.5%). Other common reasons included not trading futures yet (27.3%) and simply not knowing the feature existed (22.7%).

Willingness to let AI trade rose from 55% when only notifications were offered to 71.8% when limits on funds, positions, leverage, and losses were in place. Only 6.5% of respondents said they would allow AI to control more than half their account.

Among non-users, the most requested first steps were a clearer explanation of what the bot does (27.3%) and a trial reward for the first trade (22.7%). Half of those who had not tried an AI bot said they were ready to do so; another 36.4% wanted to learn more first.

Users who had already tried Bitrue AI most often cited time saved from watching charts, automatic execution, and market analysis as the main benefits. Requests for improvement centered on more trading pairs, flexible parameters & alerts tied to indicators such as RSI.

The report profiles eight systems that illustrate different approaches:

AI automation continues to expand, but adoption still hinges on control. Crypto traders want to see why a strategy was chosen, know the maximum loss, test it first, and understand connection security and costs.

Tools that explain their reasoning, enforce user-set boundaries, and allow small or reversible starts are the ones positioned to convert interest into regular use. The report does not forecast specific outcomes beyond these observed trends.

The numbers show both rapid builder activity and cautious but growing trader demand. The gap between the two is being closed by guardrails, explanations, and simpler interfaces rather than by handing full control to AI.

#5136. OmenX announces $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures and launches on-demand 30-second Bitcoin predictions

Strict editorial policy that focuses on accuracy, relevance, and impartiality

Toronto, November 19, 2026 – OmenX, a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform, today announced $2 million in funding from Informed Ventures alongside the launch of its on-demand, 30-second Bitcoin price prediction product.

The new product lets users predict whether Bitcoin’s price will rise or fall over the next 30 seconds, with each trade starting its own prediction window. A position opened at 10:00:12 runs until 10:00:42. Users can act when their view forms, with a full 30-second horizon, rather than adapting to the remaining time in a shared market round.

Featuring zero-slippage execution and rapid settlement, the product extends the familiar five- and fifteen-minute crypto prediction format to a shorter, individually timed experience. It adds to OmenX’s intraday offering, which spans prediction horizons from 30 seconds to 24 hours, depending on the market.

Beyond crypto, OmenX offers directional prediction markets linked to more than 100 global assets, including U.S. equities, futures, ETFs and indices. Its event markets also cover live sports and esports, with sports coverage spanning major football leagues, basketball, American football, ice hockey, baseball and UFC.

Leverage has been central to OmenX’s platform from the outset, allowing traders to amplify their exposure on supported event markets. The latest launch builds on that foundation while advancing a broader goal: making prediction markets a practical financial tool for retail users.

OmenX organizes the trading decision around a defined question: will an asset’s price be higher or lower at the end of a specified period? Users can express a directional view without purchasing the underlying asset, targeting an exact closing price or constructing an options position that requires decisions about strikes, implied volatility and time decay.

“Leverage has been part of OmenX from the start, but our ambition goes beyond adding leverage to prediction markets,” said James, founder and CEO of OmenX. “We want to make global markets easier to participate in. A trader should be able to take a view on Bitcoin, a stock or a sporting event and express it through a clear contract and a timeframe that fits their judgment.”

The platform’s emphasis on short, recurring markets provides faster feedback on trading decisions and can reduce the time capital remains committed to individual outcomes. OmenX plans to expand its coverage of traditional and crypto assets while deepening the trading experience across supported markets.

OmenX is a Base-native leveraged prediction market platform covering crypto, global financial assets, live sports and esports. Through defined outcomes, short settlement cycles and leverage on supported markets, OmenX is building a more accessible way to trade market views.

AutomatenSpieleX focuses on creating transparent reviews to help players make better choices. Here, we look at the criteria the site uses to evaluate these casinos.

With hundreds of online casinos available to Canadians, choosing a platform can be difficult. Casino reviews help players compare their options by providing information on key features, strengths, limitations, and overall quality. Rankings can also make it easier to narrow down the available choices.

With that said, there are concerns when it comes to relying on casino reviews. Players may be exposed to biased details, in which case reviews may focus on specific partnerships instead of offering transparent information about online casinos. This is why careful research is needed before deciding which of these sources to trust when researching casinos.

AutomatenSpieleX is an established online casino guide and review platform that focuses on transparency, honesty, and helping Canadians navigate the landscape safely. Users can access a great variety of resources, including guides on casino bonuses, games, and specific platforms.

AutomatenSpieleX explains the criteria used to evaluate and rate online casinos. This gives Canadian players a clearer understanding of what each rating is based on and which factors matter when comparing platforms.

Each review considers several key areas, which we examine below.

Licensing and player safety are among the first areas AutomatenSpieleX checks when reviewing a casino. The process starts with identifying the operator behind the platform and verifying its licensing information.

Operator details are usually available in the website footer or terms and conditions. This information helps reviewers identify the company responsible for the casino and check its licensing status and background.

Canadian players may encounter casinos regulated by different authorities, depending on where the operator is based and where it offers its services. AutomatenSpieleX checks the relevant licence and whether the casino is permitted to accept players from the applicable Canadian market.

Technical security is also reviewed. This includes checking whether the casino uses a valid SSL/TLS certificate to encrypt data transmitted between the player’s browser and the website.

Casino bonuses can add value to a deposit, but the advertised amount does not tell the full story. AutomatenSpieleX evaluates promotions based on both their value and the conditions attached to them.

For deposit bonuses, the review considers the match percentage and maximum bonus amount. A 100% match is common, although some casinos offer higher percentages or separate promotions for crypto deposits. Welcome packages may also include free spins, and existing players can often access reload bonuses or other ongoing offers.

The terms are just as important as the headline value. A large deposit match may be less attractive if it comes with high wagering requirements or strict withdrawal conditions. AutomatenSpieleX reviews these requirements alongside other restrictions to give Canadian players a clearer idea of how practical each bonus is to use.

Another thing that experts at AutomatenSpieleX consider during the review process is the games players can access at these online casinos. In addition to the specific titles, it’s important to look at the actual software providers the casino works with. When casinos host games from big providers, such as Pragmatic Play, NetEnt, and Yggdrasil Gaming, it generally adds more trust to the operator’s name. These companies are often selective about which operators and casinos they decide to work with.

When it comes to slots in particular, the focus is on understanding the fairness and features. Important considerations include:

AutomatenSpieleX also reviews the payment options available at each casino, with a focus on convenience and flexibility for Canadian players. Alongside credit and debit cards, casinos may support e-wallets and cryptocurrencies.

The review considers more than the number of available methods. Minimum deposit and withdrawal amounts can vary between payment options, so players should check the limits that apply to their preferred method.

Fees are another factor. Some casinos process deposits and withdrawals without additional charges, but this is not universal. Payment providers may also apply their own fees. AutomatenSpieleX considers these costs together with transaction limits, supported currencies, and processing times when evaluating a casino’s payment options.

For Canadian players who access casinos from a smartphone, mobile performance is another relevant part of the review. AutomatenSpieleX looks at whether the main casino features remain accessible on a smaller screen. Players should be able to browse games, manage their account, make payments, claim available promotions, and request withdrawals without switching to a desktop computer.

#5132. Bitcoin flashes a signal seen at four previous market bottoms as $62,000 comes under pressure

Glassnode saw losses at levels associated with past bottoms, while CryptoQuant’s 30-day total remains below the losses recorded at February and June lows.

The Bitcoin rebound from just above $62,000 was weaker the second time. The bounces came on Nov. 15 and 18, and the second session closed closer to its low. By then, a CryptoQuant measure showed the steepest losses since mid-August on older coins that moved. The next question is whether spot buyers can absorb that pressure for more than a day.

The Nov. 15 and Nov. 18 lows were $62,006 and $62,063 on the daily candles. Bitcoin finished the first day at $65,351 and the second at $63,068.

In a Nov. 19 analysis for CryptoQuant, Woominkyu put 30-day net realized losses at $8 billion, well short of two earlier 2026 readings. Glassnode’s Nov. 17 report found losses at levels it had seen around past market bottoms when measured against a year’s worth of realized profits.

Both gauges start from an estimate of what investors gained or lost when coins moved. Glassnode compares realized losses with profits taken over the previous year. On that relative measure, the weekend selloff reached readings Glassnode associated with lows in 2018, 2020, 2022 and early 2023.

Glassnode’s ratio reached levels seen near past lows. CryptoQuant’s 30-day net loss was smaller than in February or June.

A steep wave of losses can stand out against past profits even when the 30-day net dollar loss is smaller than in earlier selloffs.

The Glassnode article specifies the profit lookback. It leaves the exact loss window unstated. Both measures describe past coin movements.

The left branch shows Glassnode’s ratio of realized losses to prior-year realized profits. The right branch shows CryptoQuant’s rolling 30-day net realized profit or loss. The branch layout is conceptual.

The Glassnode article specifies the profit lookback. It leaves the exact loss window unstated. Both measures describe past coin movements.

CryptoQuant’s series tallies profits and subtracts losses over a rolling 30-day period. On that measure, net losses hit $30 billion on Feb. 20 and $18 billion on June 30. Even with a smaller monthly reading, losses were concentrated in the latest selloff. The four days from Nov. 15 to Nov. 18 produced $5 billion in net losses, more than half the 30-day figure.

Thanks for signing up to The Catalyst. Look out for your first daily email. If you already receive it, you’re all set.

A burst of losses can look extreme against a year’s profits while the month’s net dollar loss stays smaller than it was in a previous selloff. Earlier gains still in the 30-day window can offset part of the recent losses. Neither gauge sets a threshold Bitcoin has to reach before the price can stabilize.

Woominkyu’s Nov. 19 CryptoQuant Quicktake lists net losses of $30 billion on Feb. 20, $18.4 billion on June 30, and $8.4 billion in its latest reading.

That pressure reached coins that had been idle for more than 155 days. CryptoQuant’s long-term-holder spent output profit ratio fell to 0.73 on Nov. 18, its lowest since mid-August, according to Woominkyu’s analysis. The reading implies roughly 73 cents in value when those outputs moved for each dollar of value when they were created. The series measures only older outputs that moved, including transfers that can occur without a trade on an exchange.

The spot market gave a more tentative signal. Glassnode saw Bitcoin briefly trade at a premium on Coinbase around the Nov. 15 low before slipping back to a discount. Woominkyu put the Nov. 18 reading for CryptoQuant’s Coinbase Premium Index at minus 0.14%. That index compares the dollar price on Coinbase with the USDT price on Binance. It helps gauge relative buying pressure across venues using prices alone.

Glassnode also reported that buyer-initiated spot trades outweighed seller-initiated trades over the day leading into its Nov. 17 snapshot. Sustained buying in completed spot trades would give the rebound more weight. Standing buy orders can still be withdrawn.

The New York Fed calendar scheduled initial jobless claims and the Philadelphia Fed manufacturing survey for 8:30 a.m. ET on Nov. 19. Because the reports share a release time, a move in the two-year Treasury yield could reflect either or both. The yield was 4.80% on Nov. 18, unchanged from the day before in the Treasury’s daily series.

Bitcoin can respond quickly to a change in rate expectations. Daily on-chain readings take longer to fill in. If Bitcoin’s price stays above the recent lows, watch whether daily net losses ease and the older-coin ratio moves back toward 1, where spending and creation values are equal. A narrower Coinbase discount alongside sustained spot buying would add evidence that buyers can absorb the supply. A daily close near $62,000 while losses deepen and the discount persists would leave the rebound on weaker footing.

#5131. XRP Outperforms Solana and Dogecoin in Japan

Although XRP is at risk of losing its top-four position in the global cryptocurrency market, the asset still ranks among the three largest crypto assets in Japan.

In a recent post shared by the renowned Ripple-backed XRP treasury firm Evernorth, the company highlighted XRP’s growing performance in the Japan crypto market.

Earlier today, Evernorth shared monthly data from the Japan Virtual and Crypto Assets Exchange Association (JVCEA) revealing that XRP recorded about ¥132.8 billion in spot trading volume in September 2026.

While this accounted for about 15% of Japan's total crypto spot trading volume during the month, XRP emerged as the third most-traded cryptocurrency in Japan after Bitcoin and Ethereum.

This shows that XRP has outperformed other major altcoins that are currently trading in the Japan crypto market, hitting about $880 million in trading volume.

While further data showed Solana and Dogecoin ranking next to XRP on the list as the fourth- and fifth-largest cryptocurrencies in Japan, respectively, the data also showed a wide gap from XRP’s ¥132.8 billion spot volume.

This means that XRP is significantly ahead of Solana and Dogecoin in the Japan crypto trading market, as Solana recorded only about ¥19.47 billion in trading volume during the same month.

Dogecoin, on the other hand, saw less participation, as it recorded only ¥11.27 billion in spot volume during the same period.

With XRP sitting in the third spot, the asset has become one of the most actively traded cryptocurrencies in Japan despite its persistent price volatility.

#5130. CoinShares sells $19.3M in ETH and SOL – What’s behind the move?

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

Read the best crypto stories of the day in less than 5 minutes. Join to get it daily in your inbox.

CoinShares has revealed that in October, it sold its entire Ethereum [ETH] treasury position and half of its Solana [SOL] holdings.

The European digital asset manager’s ETH sale brought in $16.6 million, and its SOL sale added another $2.7 million. That’s $19.3 million put together, and none of it is going back to crypto.

Instead, CoinShares is using it to buy back its own stock.

On the 22nd of October, the board cleared up to $40 million for buybacks. This one sale covers close to half of that budget.

The company shared the details in its Q3 results this week. CEO Jean-Maria Mognetti described the sale as a way to keep cash on hand, so CoinShares can step in and buy when the moment is right.

…nearly half of the $40 million authorized by the Board and gives us the flexibility to act when conditions allow.

Revenue at $27.7 million is about 45% lower than a year ago. What rescued the quarter was the company’s own crypto. Holdings gained $14.4 million in value; it was a nice turnaround from the $5.4 million hit it took in Q2.

However, there were some bright spots. Lending and trading picked up, so capital markets income went up to $17.8 million. That’s nearly 4x the previous quarter! Operating income also bounced back after a loss in Q2.

Zooming out, though, makes things appear weaker. EBITDA fell 61.4% YoY to $20.6 million. Notably, net income for the first nine months was $15.6 million, compared with $108.8 million at this point last year.

Money kept coming in, even if fees didn’t show it.

CoinShares’ investment products had inflows worth $125 million in Q3. Management fees stayed flat at $19.1 million, since crypto prices were sluggish until late September.

They launched a Bitcoin mining ETF for European institutions in July and bought Quant Manager Bastion in September.

December’s the next big step, though. CoinShares is set to join nine Russell indices, including the Russell 2000. Funds worth about $789.9 billion track these indices. If confirmed, the change takes effect after markets close on the 11th of December.

#5129. Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » Bitcoin Is Calmer Than 19% of S&P 500 Stocks, But Here’s a Catch

Grayscale’s latest report highlights a hidden risk that still catches market-timing investors off guard.

New research from Grayscale shows Bitcoin’s (BTC) volatility has fallen to roughly 43%—lower than nearly one in five S&P 500 stocks.

The catch? Bitcoin’s calmer day-to-day trading hides a massive trap for anyone trying to time dips: almost all of its multi-year gains still come from just a handful of explosive trading days.

In its report, “Beyond Volatility: Rethinking Cryptocurrency Risks,” US digital asset manager Grayscale says Bitcoin’s long-term performance is heavily influenced by a handful of trading days. Its returns have “fat tails,” meaning sharp gains and losses occur more frequently than in traditional stocks.

Over the past three years, Bitcoin delivered an annualized return of roughly 60%. Excluding its 10 best days would have cut that figure to 7%, while excluding its 10 worst days would have raised it to 197%.

The report also notes that Bitcoin has historically rebounded sharply after major declines. Since 2011, it has experienced seven drawdowns exceeding 50%, although Grayscale says these declines are not unusually severe compared with stocks and bonds when adjusted for volatility.

Grayscale also sees Bitcoin as a potential portfolio diversifier because it is less exposed to traditional market factors.

The company points out that Bitcoin has historically recovered sharply after significant declines. Since 2011, Bitcoin has experienced seven drawdowns of more than 50% from previous highs.

The report cites Bitcoin’s inclusion in J.P. Morgan Asset Management’s 2027 Long-Term Capital Market Assumptions as a milestone.

Grayscale describes JPMorgan as a $5 trillion investment manager that now examines Bitcoin alongside established asset classes.

The banks’ 10-year base case for Bitcoin projects a 10% compound annualized return for Bitcoin over the next decade, the highest among the asset classes covered. The forecast also assumes 55% annualized volatility and a 33% correlation with US large-cap stocks, the number below international equities, corporate bonds and hedge funds.

In Bitcoin’s early years, volatility routinely exceeded 100% and at times approached 200%, with a market cap in the single-digit billions.

Grayscale ties the decline to roughly 43% to larger market value and liquidity, greater institutional participation, Bitcoin exchange-traded products and regulatory clarity.

In historical tests, modest Bitcoin allocations raised annualized return and Sharpe ratio in a representative institutional portfolio.

Over three years, Bitcoin explained about half of return variation across FTSE Grayscale Crypto Sectors. Among the 10 largest non-stablecoin assets, six led quarterly performance over the past two years, while Bitcoin led none.

JPMorgan’s decision to include Bitcoin in its long-term forecasts, along with declining volatility, could shape how institutions approach crypto investments. At the same time, Grayscale’s data shows how much Bitcoin’s long-term performance depends on a small number of trading days, highlighting the risks of trying to time the market.

PANAMA CITY, November 19, 2026 – BingX, the world’s leading multi-asset trading platform, today announced that Anthropic (Nasdaq: ANT) is available for trading on its platform following the company’s highly anticipated initial public offering. Eligible users can trade ANT/USDT on BingX Spot or take long and short positions through USDT-margined ANTUS(ANTHROPIC) Perpetual Futures. The launch extends BingX’s Anthropic trading offering from pre-IPO exposure to markets linked to its publicly listed stock.

Anthropic’s public listing marks a major milestone for the developer of Claude and brings one of the world’s most closely watched AI companies to public markets. At the 2026 Breakpoint event, Brennan Watt, CEO of Anza, gave a walkthrough of Solana’s wins this year, while sharing what is in store for 2027.

According to Watt, 2026 was a major year for Solana as it migrated its consensus to Alpenglow, slashed the block times in half from 400 ms to 200 ms while doubling capacity.

The Alpenglow upgrade went live on mainnet on October 21, 2026, cutting transaction finality from about 12.8 seconds down to roughly 150 milliseconds. It replaced TowerBFT with Votor, a faster path to reaching agreement.

After Alpenglow, @bw_solana laid out @anza_xyz roadmap for Solana in 2027 Performance: network compute capacity doubles, transactions cut 80% CU units for token accounts Expressivity: vector processing for models running fully onchain, 64 → 96 accounts per transaction, read account data instead of copying it so less data moves per transaction Market Structure: Alpenglow. Next with faster block distribution and Constellation for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators Resilience: simpler protocol with fewer special cases, safer to change https://t.co/EpvDdSyjln

Solana recently transitioned to 1.0, marking the network’s graduation from “mainnet beta” to “mainnet” and retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch. Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience.

According to Watt, Solana is eyeing significant improvements in 2027 across four categories. First is Resilience, which involves simplifying the protocol, reducing special cases, and making it safer to change.

“So, we're going to go ahead and simplify the protocol, replacing legacy abstractions and interfaces, pushing more of the execution on chain, and modernizing some of the wire formats. And all of this, you know, enhances resiliency, but it also allows us to move quicker and be more agile and deploy things and evolve the protocol more quickly,” Watt stated.

Second is Market Structure, which centers on Alpenglow, which aims for faster block distribution, and Constellation, which aims for clearer ordering rules and more competition among validators.

“Several important Alpenglow extensions are coming,” Watt stated. Alpenglow rolls out in two phases: first is Votor, its voting protocol, which is already live on the platform; second is Rotor, a single relay layer planned for a later release that will replace Turbine, the protocol that spreads a block’s data across the network.

Third is Performance, where network compute capacity doubles and transactions use 80% fewer compute units for token accounts. Last is Expressivity, which involves vector processing for models running fully onchain and an increase from 64 to 96 accounts per transaction.

Watt also spoke about improvements in onchain development: “The cost of storing data on Solana came down by 27% this year. And just in the coming two weeks, we're going to bring this thing down by another 7x.”

#5125. Anthropic hits $1.5 trillion valuation in record IPO as ECB warns AI funding could dry up

The central bank says IPO booms have historically preceded weaker stock returns. It does not see the issuance surge as a systemic risk today.

Anthropic priced its $81 billion IPO at $83 a share Wednesday. The company behind Claude said it expected trading to begin on Nasdaq on Nov. 19. If the stock opens above $83, investors who got shares in the offering will have an immediate gain on paper. Anthropic won't get any extra cash from that move.

The net result is that Anthropic has effectively raised $81.3 billion from its public offering, with a further $26 billion private placement. This creates a $1.5 trillion fully diluted valuation despite growing concerns over AI infrastructure spending and financing risks.

The European Central Bank warned Wednesday that stock returns have tended to weaken after a rush of companies going public. Its concern is what happens when the rush ends: AI companies may still have data centers to finish and bills to pay, but could find it harder to raise cash if stock prices fall and lenders pull back. For Bitcoin and the broader crypto industry, the question is whether a pullback in AI shares becomes a wider selloff in risk assets, not whether the IPO itself takes money out of crypto.

US initial public offerings brought in about $44 billion in 2025. In its November financial stability review, the ECB cited a July analyst forecast of about $225 billion for all of 2026, alongside its staff's separate $212 billion estimate from early November. Both were made before Anthropic set its final price.

Rounded annual US IPO proceeds. 2025 is reported historical activity; the two 2026 bars are separate full-year forecasts, not additive amounts or completed offerings. The ECB staff estimate was prepared in early November using actual January–October proceeds, a seasonal forecast, and preliminary Anthropic inputs. The market-analyst projection dates to July. Both predate Anthropic’s final Nov. 18 pricing.

Source: ECB November 2026 Financial Stability Review, section 1, Chart C.3 notes and footnote 4

It's easier to see why offerings tend to bunch together from the company's side. If investors are willing to pay more for each share, a company can raise the same amount of cash by selling a smaller piece of itself. Other companies see those terms and have a reason to get their own deals done before demand cools.

The ECB compared the size of each quarter's IPOs relative to the economy with what the broader stock market returned over the next two years. In the US, higher issuance went with weaker returns, but the relationship accounted for only about a tenth of the variation. It tells us more about the conditions in which companies choose to sell shares than it does about where Anthropic will trade this afternoon.

Selling shares gives a company cash it doesn't have to repay. If the price drops, shareholders take the loss, and the company keeps the money it already raised. The trouble starts when a business still needs money to finish building and has fewer ways to raise it. Borrowers still owe interest, and AI companies can still owe rent for computing space they no longer need. When a data-center operator borrows against its tenants' payments, the people buying those data-center bonds are counting on the tenants to keep paying.

The ECB’s review of AI borrowing extends that risk beyond shareholders: if lenders start doubting projects will bring in enough cash, they can charge more or stop funding new ones, even as falling stock prices make raising money by selling shares more expensive. The ECB said the issuance surge and the rise of passive investing do not currently pose a systemic risk.

When a company goes public, it sells newly created shares to raise money, and people who already own shares can sell some of theirs in the same deal. Anthropic will be doing both.

Its final terms cover 980 million shares at $83 each. About $79 billion goes to Anthropic for the new shares and $2 billion goes to existing shareholders, before fees in both cases. That excludes an option for the banks running the deal to buy up to 147 million additional shares. Anthropic also arranged a separate $26 billion private placement with strategic partners, contingent on the IPO closing.

Gross proceeds at the $83 offer price: $79.38 billion for Anthropic and $1.96 billion for selling stockholders, totaling $81.34 billion before underwriting discounts and other expenses. Calculated from the final share allocation. Excludes the underwriters’ option to buy 147 million additional shares; does not represent money raised through subsequent Nasdaq trading.

Source: Anthropic final IPO pricing announcement, Nov. 18, 2026

Those banks are the underwriters. They take indications of how many shares investors want and what they're willing to pay, then help the company set the price and decide who gets shares. Under the deal's underwriting terms, the banks agree to buy the shares from Anthropic and the selling shareholders and resell them to investors. They're paid through a discount: the banks pay the sellers less per share than the investors pay. If you got an allocation, you were assigned a number of shares at $83. If you buy after trading starts, you pay the market price, and the money goes to the investor selling you the shares.

The money Anthropic gets from selling new stock gives it more room to pay for the equipment and computing capacity it needs to run Claude. Its IPO filing puts expected payments on contractual commitments at $71 billion over the 12 months after Sept. 30, including $4 billion tied to arrangements with conditions or termination rights. Those are primarily commitments for computing and infrastructure, not a loan coming due or a bill the IPO was specifically set up to pay.

The company also reported $147 billion in liquidity as of Sept. 30, before the IPO and private placement, so the commitments do not by themselves indicate an immediate cash shortfall. They give a sense of why access to funding counts long after the first trade. The stock is due to start trading Thursday, while Anthropic expects the offering itself to close Friday if the usual conditions are met.

Anthropic is due to trade under the ticker ANT. Nasdaq's regular session starts at 9:30 a.m. New York time, but the stock doesn't have to open at that hour. The exchange runs an opening auction for IPOs, collecting buy and sell orders and finding the price at which the most shares can change hands. The first trade tells you how that initial batch of orders matched. The closing price will show whether buyers were still willing to pay as much after a session of trading.

Index funds can bring another set of buyers later. These funds aim to match a specified list of stocks, so when an index adds a company, the funds that follow it generally adjust their holdings. MSCI says Anthropic would enter its broad investable market indexes at the Nov. 30 close, effective Dec. 1, if it qualifies for early entry. Which funds would buy depends on the exact index each one tracks.

The ECB found that companies already on the market tended to sell more stock when index funds owned a larger share of them. Its researchers think the prospect of those buyers arriving soon after listing could help some companies raise more at their IPO, too. They didn't estimate how much of Anthropic's $83 price came from that expectation.

Crypto traders already have contracts tied to Anthropic's share price. The Nasdaq debut gives them an actual share price to compare those contracts with. Bitcoin‘s 30-day correlation with the Nasdaq-100 stood at 0.7 in Talos's Nov. 12 report, pointing to sensitivity to the same shifts in investor risk appetite. But a move in both on Thursday wouldn't establish that investors sold Bitcoin to buy ANT.

Even a strong first day would tell us only what buyers were willing to pay for Anthropic now. The ECB's warning is about whether AI companies can still raise cash on reasonable terms when investors are less eager, and the bills are still coming due.
